claim: Dose per well and incubation time for the HepG2 arm of the 1,080-formulation screen
locus_A: This paper, Methods / In Vitro Transfection and Luciferase Assay: "4 uL of a particle suspension at 25 ug pDNA/mL was pipetted into 100 uL of culture media" = 0.1 ug pDNA/well, and "After 48 h of incubation"
locus_B: Nat Commun 2022, PMID 35879315, Cell culture and high-throughput screening: "8 uL of a particle suspension at 25 ug pDNA/mL was pipetted into the 200 uL culture media" = 0.2 ug pDNA/well, and "A 24 h incubation"
what_we_emitted: Dose_ug_nucleicacid = 0.1 and timepoint 48 h on the 4,680 emitted training rows, with the conflict named in curation_note on EVERY row
why: Both papers give the same FINAL concentration, 1 ug pDNA/mL, but differ 2x in per-well dose and 2x in incubation. They are describing the same physical screen: this paper's RLU_HepG2 is byte-equal to the corpus's YZ_2022 values once the 3-decimal rounding is accounted for (02b_duplicate_quantified.json). The five cell lines we emit are described ONLY by this paper, so this paper's numbers are used; but the same Methods paragraph demonstrably misdescribes the HepG2 subset, so it is not a clean authority and the rows say so. Not resolvable from either paper.

claim: The identity of the helper lipid called 18PG
locus_A: This paper, SI Table 2 (p2, image xref 68, renders/p2_x68.png): BOTH acyl tails drawn with a cis C=C; SI Table 3 prints Double_bonds = 2 for 18PG; Raw_Data/1080_LNP_OHE.csv carries Double_bonds = 2 on all 180 18PG rows. All three say 18:1/18:1 = DOPG.
locus_B: Nat Commun 2022, PMID 35879315, describing THIS SAME 1,080-formulation library: "the anionic 1,2-dimyristoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate (14PA) and 1-stearoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-(1'-rac-glycerol) (18PG)" = SOPG, 18:0/18:1, ONE C=C. provenance/reagent_registry.py pins 18PG to SOPG on that authority, across 1,474 corpus rows in WT_2026, YZ_2022 and YZ_2024.
what_we_emitted: HL_SMILES = dioleoyl PG with a 1'-rac head, DSNRWDQKZIEDDB-GCMPNPAFSA-M, on all 900 training + 72 validation 18PG rows; HL_name = 18PG as published; confidence = medium and the conflict in curation_note on every one of those 972 rows
why: One lab, one library, two mutually exclusive statements. SOPG is C42H80O10P- and DOPG is C42H78O10P-, so mass CAN see this one -- what no check could see is which paper to believe. This is the AC_2025 question (a name and a structure disagreeing), where the first confident repair put 419 measured values on the wrong molecules. Not repaired in either direction. NOTE: if the Nat Commun text is right, 1,474 EXISTING corpus rows are unaffected and only our 972 are wrong; if this paper's drawing is right, the 360 YZ_2022/YZ_2024 rows for this same library carry the wrong helper lipid today.

claim: Whether DOTAP has a defined stereocentre
locus_A: This paper, SI Table 2 (p2, image xref 64): a bold wedge to H at the propane C2.
locus_B: provenance/reagent_registry.py's DOTAP entry has NO stereocentre, and 2,564 corpus rows in six experiments carry that unspecified structure.
what_we_emitted: The registry's unspecified structure, with structure_assumed = 1 and the reason in curation_note on all 972 DOTAP rows
why: Emitting a stereo-defined DOTAP would give one reagent name two structures across experiments, which is what C17 gates. Declining to assert a stereocentre is the conservative half, and the flag makes the choice visible rather than silent. Affects an excipient's stereochemistry only, not the ionizable lipid and not any value.

claim: The PEG block length drawn for DMG-PEG2000
locus_A: SI Table 2 (p2, image xref 63): the bracket subscript reads 44
locus_B: The same drawing shows one further -CH2CH2-O- OUTSIDE the closing bracket, before the terminal -OCH3, so the molecule carries 45 ethylene oxides
what_we_emitted: PEG_SMILES with 45 ethylene oxides -- byte-identical to the structure YZ_2022/YZ_2024 already store
why: RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT. Reading the subscript as the answer gives a structure one ethylene oxide short: n=44 canonicalises to FHMUYYLWQDJUPK, n=45 to NLDCRRFPGOSAHV, and the corpus's stored DMG-PEG2000 is NLDCRRFPGOSAHV. A 44 Da error that only the InChIKey would have caught. This is a bracket-subscript instance of the name-token trap -- the printed number is not the count.

locus_B: Raw_Data/1080_LNP_OHE.csv holds values from 0.000 to 12.772, with 1,282 of 5,760 below 1.5 and 4,612 above 1.0 -- neither floored nor rescaled

claim: The direction of the C19 chain halves in our own C10 anchor for DLin-MC3-DMA
locus_A: make_reference.py, first version: MC3_LEFT written C1->C18 and appended as a branch off C19, which bonds C1 to C19
locus_B: The chemical name heptatriaconta-6,9,28,31-tetraen-19-yl requires the unsaturation at 6 and 9 counted from C1, not from the ester
what_we_emitted: The corrected anchor, with both branches written outward from C19
why: RETAINED AS A RETIRED SUSPICION because it is the trap itself: the wrong version had the correct molecular formula C43H79NO2 and the correct exact mass 641.611081 to six decimals. Only the InChIKey saw it (RBLCKFZMIVYNAG vs CLYUJYGYPALXTO). A fragment has a direction that mass cannot see. Fixed by re-deriving from the name, not by tuning until the key matched; the three seeded defects in make_reference.py --selftest now hold that gate open.
